cells.tense: Present — here, with the pen in your hand.
cells.verb: feeling what you pictured actually land as enough
cells.place: where things get set right between people
cells.ask: Let the satisfaction point somewhere. Pick up the one thing that genuinely pulls you now and move on it — not because something's owed, but because you're drawn — and the sense of things being square stays with you as you go.
cells.core:
Something you imagined being fair has become fair, and you can feel it. Not tallied — felt. You're not waiting for the last scrap to be accounted for before you let it count; what's in front of you is in proportion, and you know it in your chest, not on paper.

That kind of settled is rare and it's quiet. It also isn't a stopping place, unless you want it to be. A balance you can feel tends to want to go somewhere.
cells.sheetLine: What you pictured as fair is here, and you can feel it.

cells.tense: Future — leaning hard on a settling that hasn't settled yet.
cells.verb: insisting the fairness already feel complete
cells.place: where things get set right between people
cells.ask: Tend one thing that's still out of proportion without needing it to feel finished today — water it, leave it, come back. The fullness you're reaching for shows up on its own once what's actually happened has had time to be felt all the way through.
cells.core:
You can see the fair version so clearly that you're living in it before it's arrived. Every exchange is measured against how good it's going to feel when everything's square, and so nothing in the present is allowed to feel like enough yet — the contentment is being demanded on a schedule.

The picture isn't wrong. The timing is. Satisfaction that's being pushed ahead of the facts has a way of staying just out of reach.
cells.sheetLine: You're demanding it feel fair before it's finished balancing.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at an unfairness that's already behind you.
cells.verb: not letting yourself feel what's been made right
cells.place: where things get set right between people
cells.ask: Rather than trying to feel it, sit with what you already know: is it square now, or isn't it? Hold the answer quietly for a while without deciding what to feel about it. Feeling tends to catch up once knowing has been given room, and then the picture of fairness can rest.
cells.core:
Something got set right, and the satisfaction didn't come with it. The scales moved; you didn't. Part of you is still arguing a case that's already been decided in your favor, and so the fullness that should be here has nowhere to land.

This isn't ingratitude, and it isn't fixable by trying harder to feel glad. The feeling is downstream of something else, and that something else is what you can actually do today.
cells.sheetLine: It's been made right. You haven't let yourself feel it.

cells.tense: Disowned present — already content, still keeping score.
cells.verb: being satisfied with how it balanced out
cells.place: where things get set right between people
cells.ask: Make one careful distinction: of the things you still complain are unfair, which one is actually live, and which is a habit of counting? Say the difference to yourself, plainly. Once the real one is sorted from the reflex, what you've already felt gets to be yours — and the picture of fairness can finally match the feeling.
cells.core:
You already feel it's fair. You can tell by how little heat is actually in your voice when the subject comes up. But you keep talking as if the books were still open — listing what's still owed, holding the old grievance in place — while underneath, the matter is settled and you're at peace with it.

The contentment is doing its work. It just hasn't been given its name.
cells.sheetLine: You're already satisfied with how it came out. You're still calling it unsettled.
